evidence.source_quote: handling and storing Electro-Static Discharge (ESD) sensitive components
evidence.output_quote: R.2Outside an EPA, ESDS items are ALWAYS enclosed in closed (sealed or folded and taped) shielding packaging. Dissipative pink poly alone is not acceptable outside an EPA.

evidence.source_quote: handling and storing Electro-Static Discharge (ESD) sensitive components
evidence.output_quote: Store each PCBA individually in a closed shielding bag; unbagged PCBAs in slotted conductive racks are permitted only inside an EPA.

evidence.source_quote: handling and storing Electro-Static Discharge (ESD) sensitive components
evidence.output_quote:
ESDS item found outside EPA without shielding packaging, or in pink poly only
Do not touch it. Notify the Shift Lead. A person who passed that shift's grounding test, wearing a wrist strap connected to a portable ESD grounding (field-service) kit, encloses it in a shielding bag, touching only the package body or board edges, then quarantines it.

evidence.source_quote: handling and storing Electro-Static Discharge (ESD) sensitive components
evidence.output_quote: Test wrist strap and footwear at the personnel test station. Record PASS/FAIL, name, date and time in the ESD Test Log.

evidence.source_quote: handling and storing Electro-Static Discharge (ESD) sensitive components
evidence.output_quote:
Wrist strap system (person + strap + cord)
Each shift before EPA entry, and after any exit
< 3.5 × 10⁷ Ω (35 MΩ) on the personnel tester

evidence.source_quote: handling and storing Electro-Static Discharge (ESD) sensitive components
evidence.output_quote:
Wrist strap or footwear test FAIL
Do not enter EPA or touch exposed ESDS items. Check fit/skin contact and retest once; if still FAIL, replace strap/footwear and retest. Work resumes only after PASS.

evidence.source_quote: incorporate the operating procedures into personnel training requirements
evidence.output_quote: No person handles exposed ESDS items or works unescorted in an EPA until they complete initial ESD training covering this SOP, IPC-A-610G Section 3 handling principles, symbols, packaging and the Section 8 actions, and pass a written/practical check.

evidence.source_quote: incorporate the operating procedures into personnel training requirements
evidence.output_quote: Confirms only trained, authorized staff handle ESDS items; checks daily test log completion; stops work on any failed control; escorts visitors in EPAs.

evidence.source_quote: incorporate the operating procedures into personnel training requirements
evidence.output_quote:
Visitor / untrained person needs to enter EPA
Escort required; visitor wears a smock and tested heel grounders/footwear (Section 9), does not touch ESDS items or packaging, and stays clear of open ESDS work.

evidence.source_quote: Utilize the following standard as reference: PC-A-610G  Acceptability of Electronic Assemblies
evidence.output_quote: R.3Never touch ESDS leads, pins, connectors or board conductors. Handle by the package body or board edges, wearing clean ESD-safe gloves or finger cots where required (IPC-A-610G Section 3 handling considerations).

evidence.source_quote: Utilize the following standard as reference: PC-A-610G  Acceptability of Electronic Assemblies
evidence.output_quote: IPC-A-610G, Acceptability of Electronic Assemblies – Section 3, Handling Electronic Assemblies: EOS/ESD prevention, warning labels, protective materials, EOS/ESD-safe workstation/EPA, and handling considerations (physical damage, contamination, gloves and finger cots).

evidence.source_quote: Utilize the following standard as reference: PC-A-610G  Acceptability of Electronic Assemblies
evidence.output_quote: R.3Never touch ESDS leads, pins, connectors or board conductors. Handle by the package body or board edges, wearing clean ESD-safe gloves or finger cots where required (IPC-A-610G Section 3 handling considerations).

evidence.source_quote: handling and storage of ESD-sensitive items
evidence.output_quote:
7.4 Picking, Kitting and Issue
Pick the sealed package from storage. Split quantities (kitting, partial issue) only at an EPA bench while grounded.

evidence.source_quote: handling and storage of ESD-sensitive items
evidence.output_quote:
6. CORE RULES (APPLY AT ALL TIMES)
R.1ESDS items are removed from shielding packaging ONLY inside an EPA, by a grounded person who has passed the grounding test for that shift.

evidence.source_quote: handling and storage of ESD-sensitive items
evidence.output_quote: Do not use tape directly on ESDS items or boards. Apply labels to the sealed bag, never to the item, and do not write on a bag that is pressed against exposed parts.

evidence.source_quote: handling and storage of ESD-sensitive items
evidence.output_quote:
7.3 Storage
Store ESDS items only in the designated ESDS storage locations (marked with ESD signage and listed in the warehouse location system), in closed shielding packaging or closed conductive bins/totes.

evidence.source_quote: handling and storage of ESD-sensitive items
evidence.output_quote: Store ESDS items only in the designated ESDS storage locations (marked with ESD signage and listed in the warehouse location system), in closed shielding packaging or closed conductive bins/totes.

evidence.source_quote: handling and storage of ESD-sensitive items
evidence.output_quote: Do not over-fill bins or place heavy items on top of ESDS packages; avoid crushing leads and boards. Store each PCBA individually in a closed shielding bag; unbagged PCBAs in slotted conductive racks are permitted only inside an EPA.

evidence.source_quote: incorporate the operating procedures into personnel training requirements and daily processes
evidence.output_quote:
11. RECORDS
ESD Test Log, Verification log, calibration records, EPA audit reports, NCRs, visitor log and training records are retained for a minimum of three years or per the company record-retention policy, whichever is longer.

evidence.output_quote: Non-conductive material that holds charge: ordinary plastic bags, bubble wrap, foam, Styrofoam, tape, paper cups, clipboards, personal items.

honored.consequence: While the SOP explicitly allows closed conductive bins/totes and dissipative trays/tubes, it never mentions or recommends conductive foam inserts for storage organization (only mentioning ordinary insulating foam as a prohibited material).
honored.minimum_correction: Add conductive foam inserts/trays as an approved or recommended option for organizing and protecting component leads during storage inside closed shielding/conductive containers.

counterevidence.source_quote: handling and storage of ESD-sensitive items
counterevidence.output_quote: Pink/‘antistatic’ poly and dissipative trays/tubes. Do not generate much charge but do NOT shield. Acceptable only inside an EPA.

task_fulfillment.rationale: The deliverable is a comprehensive, well-structured, and internally consistent 4-page Word SOP for handling and storing ESD-sensitive items in warehouse operations, properly referencing IPC-A-610G and ANSI/ESD S20.20. All operative tables, exception routes, and procedures align with the core rules without contradictions. Only one minor non-critical specific item (conductive foam inserts in R43) was omitted, though closed conductive bins/totes and dissipative trays were covered.
